metadata.title: Formal Verification of the Midgard Protocol in Lean4

nodes.name: Computational Relation
nodes.statement: A relation \(\mathcal{R} \subseteq E \times A \times S \times S \) is computational if and only if there is a function \(f : E \times A \times S \to S_{\mathsf{Errors}}\) such that \[ \forall (e \in E) (a \in A) (s_{i}, s_{o} \in S), (e, a, s_{i}, s_{o}) \in \mathcal{R} \iff f(e,a,s_{i}) = \eta(s_{o}) \]
nodes.label: dfn:computational_relation

nodes.name: From Initial State
nodes.statement: Given a State Machine \(\mathsf{sm}\), we say that a state \(s\) is reach from the initial state \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) if there are 0 or more \(\mathsf{sm}\)-steps from \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) to \(s\).
nodes.label: dfn:ComputationalRelation.StateMachine.FromInit

nodes.name: After Initial State
nodes.statement: Given a State Machine \(\mathsf{sm}\), we say that a state \(s\) is reach from the initial state \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) if there are 1 or more \(\mathsf{sm}\)-steps from \(\mathsf{sm.init}\) to \(s\).
nodes.label: dfn:ComputationalRelation.StateMachine.AfterInit

nodes.name: Induction Step Machine
nodes.statement: Given a predicate that is valid for the initial state and as an invariant over the relation steps, we can prove the predicate holds for all reachable states.
nodes.label: dfn:Relations.StepMachines.ApplyInd

nodes.statement: {Transaction Information} Transaction are a tuple providing: \begin{description} \item[validity internal] execution time bounds. When missing, they are assumed to by minus infinity and plus infinity. \item[value] the amount of value in the transaction \item[fee] the fee of the transaction \item[validator] who is signing the transaction \item[transaction id] \end{description}
nodes.label: dfn:InputInfo

nodes.name: Tokens
nodes.statement: Tokens are structures containing a name, (polymorphic) data and id. Tokens are records with: \begin{description} \item[id] same as its reference \item[data] keeping internal data \item[name] the name of the token \end{description}
nodes.label: dfn:Tokens.Elem.TokenD

nodes.name: List Element
nodes.statement: List nodes are records with: \begin{description} \item[key] (optional) indicates the current node key, \item[link] (optional) indicates the next key in the list, \item[data] polymorphic element depending on the use of the list. \end{description}
nodes.label: dfn:MUList.State.Elemt

nodes.name: Onchain Lists
nodes.statement: Lists are defined as a collection of \(\textsf{Tokens}\) with internal data \(\textsf{Elemt}\) Internally, these collections are mechanized as maps from \(\textsf{TId}\) to \(\textsf{Tokens}\) or burnt tokens.
nodes.label: dfn:MUList.State.ListToken

nodes.name: Actions
nodes.statement: We have the following actions. \begin{description} \item[Modify Data] modifies the data field of a node in the list \item[Unsafe Append] adds an element at the end of the list \item[Unsafe Prepend] adds an element at the beginning of the list \item[Remove] removes an element from the list \end{description}

nodes.name: Operator Directory
nodes.statement: We define operators directory as three lists: one unordered for registered operators, and two ordered for active and retired operators.
nodes.label: dfn:OperatorDirectory.State.OperatorDirectory

nodes.name: State Transitions
nodes.statement: Operators can perform the following actions: \begin{description} \item[Activate] activates registered operators \item[Retire] retires active operators \item[Register] registers an operator by placing a bond, the operator is the one forging the transaction. \item[Deregister] deregisters an operator (if possible) \item[RemoveDuplicateSlashBond] removes fraudulent operator \item[RecoverBond] returns (if possible) the bond to a retired operator \item[ActRemoveOperatorBad] removes a fraudulent active operators, used by BadSettlement and BadBlock \item[UpdateBondHold] updates bond holding time, used by New State and New Settlement \item[RetRemove] removes fraudulent retired operators, used by Bad State and Settlement. \end{description}
nodes.label: dfn:OperatorDirectory.StateMachine.State.OperActions

nodes.name: Register Queue Violation Detection
nodes.statement: Finds if there are two elements in the registered queue with the same key and different times or there is an operator registered and active or registered and retired. Here we assume agents have a valid state of the onchain data structure.
nodes.label: dfn:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness

nodes.statement: The witness found generates a \emph{valid witness}. It finds two different tokens with matching keys.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_valid

nodes.statement: The witness found identified a registered operator to penalized. In other words, the operator to penalize is a member of the registered operator list.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_key

nodes.statement: The witness found has a valid anchor for the operator the system is penalizing.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_registered

nodes.name: Duplicate Registered Detection
nodes.statement: If the witness found is marked as registered duplication, then the witness has two distinct tokens showing duplication of a registered operator and another registered operator.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_dup_reg

nodes.name: Duplicate Registered and Active Detection

nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_dup_act

nodes.name: Duplicate Registered and Retired Detection

nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness_dup_ret

nodes.name: No Witness Detected

nodes.name: Proof Generation
nodes.statement: Takes the witness generated by the condition checker and forms a valid Midgard Operator Directory action.
nodes.label: dfn:OpsDir.OptimisticProof.GenerateFraudProof

nodes.name: Enabled Register Fraudulent Witness Submission
nodes.statement: If we find a witness(see Definition~\ref{dfn:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness}) and we can submit a transaction to L1, then we can generate a \emph{valid} action (using Definition~\ref{dfn:OpsDir.OptimisticProof.GenerateFraudProof}) having Midgard penalizing the duplicated registered operator.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticProof.EnabledFPSubmission

nodes.name: Not same Witness
nodes.statement: Let \(s_{i},s_{o}\) be two operators directory such that \(s_{o}\) is the resulting state after slashing a fraudulent operator detected in \(s_{i}\). Then, we won't find the same witness of fraudulent condition~(Def.~\ref{dfn:OpsDir.OptimisticDetection.find_witness}).
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticProof.AfterFP

nodes.name: Disabled Duplicate Submission
nodes.statement: If when we check, we do not find any duplicates in the registered operators queue, nor intersections with the retired and active queues, then in the current state, Midgard does not accept the removal of registered operators accused of being duplicated.
nodes.label: thm:OpsDir.OptimisticProof.DisableFPSubmittion

nodes.name: Scheduler State
nodes.statement: The scheduler state is simply a record of values: \begin{description} \item[operator\_id] indicating the current operator's id \item[shift\_start] indicating when the shift starts. \end{description}
nodes.label: dfn:Scheduler.State.SchedulerDatum

nodes.statement: State machine producing the next state triggered by two operations: \begin{enumerate} \item Advance \item Rewind \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: Similar to the state transition function.

nodes.name: Shifts progresses by shift duration
nodes.statement: At each step, the new shift starts when the previous ended shifted by \emph{shift\_duration}.
nodes.label: thm:Scheduler.Properties.ShiftStepShiftInterval

nodes.statement: The scheduler chooses operators from the active queue in the operator directory.

nodes.name: Self Claim Scheduler without Rewinding
nodes.statement: Assuming we can build a transaction \(\mathsf{tx}\) such that the time validity bounds in \(\mathsf{tx}\) fit inside the interval \([ \mathsf{sch.shift\_start} + \mathsf{shift\_duration} , \mathsf{sch.shift\_start} + 2*\mathsf{shift\_duration})\), then the next operator in line can claim control of the scheduler.
nodes.label: thm:Scheduler.Properties.ClaimScheduler

nodes.name: Scheduler Rewinds
nodes.statement: The last active operator rewinds the scheduler when there are no registered operators waiting to be activated.
nodes.label: thm:Scheduler.Properties.ClaimSchedulerRewind

nodes.statement: {Confirmed State} Confirmed States are records containing the initial starting time of the protocol, the last recorded end time (last's confirmed block end time), the last confirmed block previous hash, the last confirmed block hash, the root of the merkle tree representing the set of UTXOs, and the protocol version.
